page: Amazon Web Services a1.xlarge is an ARM-based virtual machine instance powered by the first-generation AWS Graviton processor. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, this instance features 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs using the ARMv8 Cortex-A72 architecture running at 2.3 GHz. It is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core, and does not include local storage or GPU hardware. Network connectivity is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the first-generation Graviton architecture delivers modest performance compared to modern x86 or newer ARM iterations. The instance achieves an average rating in stress-ng single-core CPU performance with a score of 1488.48, but drops to a weak rating of 5919.11 in multi-core execution. Memory subsystem performance is constrained, with uncached large-block read and write bandwidths measuring 12.56 GB/sec and 6.77 GB/sec respectively, both falling into the bottom 10% tier. Similarly, Geekbench scores reflect entry-level capabilities, yielding a single-core score of 408.0 and a multi-core score of 1245.0.

The primary tradeoff of the a1.xlarge is its limited instruction set and lower computational throughput, lacking advanced vector extensions (AVX), matrix extensions (AMX), or hyperthreading. However, its dedicated core allocation and ARM architecture offer a cost-efficient entry point for testing and compiling ARM64 applications. It is appropriate for lightweight, scale-out workloads such as basic web serving, development and testing environments, and simple containerized microservices that do not require high memory bandwidth or intensive floating-point calculations.
